entities.summary: Louise Joséphine Bourgeois was a French-American artist. Although she is best known for her large-scale sculpture and installation art, Bourgeois was also a prolific painter and printmaker. She explored a variety of themes over the course of her long career including domesticity and the family, sexuality and the body, as well as death and the unconscious. These themes connect to events from her childhood which she considered to be a therapeutic process. Although Bourgeois exhibited with the abstract expressionists and her work has a lot in common with Surrealism and feminist art, she was not formally affiliated with a particular artistic movement.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a pioneering feminist artist, Louise Bourgeois's work challenged traditional notions of femininity and domesticity, influencing generations of artists and women's rights activists. Her exploration of themes such as the body, sexuality, and death has had a lasting impact on modern art and culture.
